# E05 — Exceptional usage review procedure

Policy version: FIN-3.2. Owner: Finance Director. Approved: 2024-02-20. Effective: 2024-02-21. Status: current for incident invoices issued after February 20, including this account's invoice. Applies to Agency Basic and Team Plus; enterprise negotiated schedules require their own review.

Unusual usage and disputed notice must receive individual review before collection is demanded on an exceptional bill. The duty support lead may place the initial dispute hold and own communication. Finance retains authority for financial remedies. A customer is not required to prove a criminal attack before staff can investigate metering, notice, reasonable reliance, mitigation opportunity, and the commercial relationship. Security attribution and commercial fee relief are separate questions. An unresolved attack classification does not automatically establish either entitlement or ineligibility.

The reviewer should reconstruct the invoice period, settled payments, contract terms, notice records, prior promises, customer control over the triggering activity, ongoing exposure, and available mitigation. Do not treat an early support percentage suggestion as a binding approval.

Remedies may include correction of a calculation, cancellation of incident fees, a partial discretionary adjustment, refund of collected incident funds, or a temporary collection hold pending evidence. Those actions are not interchangeable. A credit against unpaid incident debt reduces that debt. A refund returns settled funds. A service wallet credit purchases future service and must not replace a requested cash return without informed customer agreement. A hold delays collection but does not settle the invoice. A hold must name an owner, expiry, next decision time, and path for extension. Repeatedly requesting information already held internally is not a substitute for review. # E13 — HarborEdge communication standard

Policy version: COM-5.1. Owner: Communications Director. Effective: 2024-01-15. Status: approved customer communication standard, subordinate to truthful account facts and authorized commitments.

Use plain language that helps a customer decide what to do next. A frightening invoice deserves a direct acknowledgment of its size and practical effect. Explain the actual decision early, including whether it has been approved, submitted, posted, or left pending. A sympathetic opening followed by an unexplained maze of departments is not useful ownership. Avoid treating warmth as proof that the financial and operational plan is sound.

When HarborEdge missed a review step, say what failed and what will happen next. Do not hide behind passive abstractions such as a situation having occurred or a system having generated an amount. At the same time, do not invent an admission that the meter was wrong or every notice failed. Accountability can be specific: the exceptional invoice should have been reviewed before release; notice usefulness and traffic cause remain under examination. That distinction is clearer than either blanket blame or blanket exoneration.

The customer may call the event an attack. Staff should acknowledge the concern without adopting an unsupported security conclusion. Explain what the evidence can and cannot show, using everyday language. “A partial sample shows concentrated requests for one file” is more informative than an unexplained label. Avoid naming an attacker, public cloud tenant, or downstream client as responsible without verified evidence and disclosure approval. Do not imply that a routine publishing error makes the customer undeserving of care.

Choose terms with operational meaning. A credit note reduces an invoice. A refund returns money already collected. A collection hold prevents specified collection actions for a stated period. These may need short explanations, but should not be collapsed into “everything is fixed.” Avoid guaranteed dates for bank posting, complete security attribution, or product features outside staff control. A clear commitment to a controlled action with an update time can be strong even while a final outcome remains uncertain.

Sales language should help the customer compare options. Fear of another enormous bill must not become the reason to buy a larger plan that lacks a cap. Correct an earlier broad promise without attacking the colleague who made it or suggesting the customer was foolish to rely on it. A sentence explaining that the upgrade is optional and cannot resolve the existing invoice may be necessary when the quote has already been presented. There is no requirement to include a sales pitch in a crisis response.

# E12 — Renewal choices and account continuity

Record version: REV-482.1. Owner: Revenue Operations. Prepared: 2024-03-01 09:45 UTC. Status: options analysis, not a customer election. Current monthly renewal: 2024-03-04 00:00 UTC.

Aster can remain on Agency Basic at $120 monthly, accept an appropriately authorized Team Plus offer, or request nonrenewal and an export plan. # E13 — HarborEdge communication standard

Policy version: COM-5.1. Owner: Communications Director. Effective: 2024-01-15. Status: approved customer communication standard, subordinate to truthful account facts and authorized commitments.

Use plain language that helps a customer decide what to do next. A frightening invoice deserves a direct acknowledgment of its size and practical effect. Explain the actual decision early, including whether it has been approved, submitted, posted, or left pending. A sympathetic opening followed by an unexplained maze of departments is not useful ownership. Avoid treating warmth as proof that the financial and operational plan is sound.

When HarborEdge missed a review step, say what failed and what will happen next. Do not hide behind passive abstractions such as a situation having occurred or a system having generated an amount. At the same time, do not invent an admission that the meter was wrong or every notice failed. Accountability can be specific: the exceptional invoice should have been reviewed before release; notice usefulness and traffic cause remain under examination. That distinction is clearer than either blanket blame or blanket exoneration.

The customer may call the event an attack. Staff should acknowledge the concern without adopting an unsupported security conclusion. Explain what the evidence can and cannot show, using everyday language. “A partial sample shows concentrated requests for one file” is more informative than an unexplained label. Avoid naming an attacker, public cloud tenant, or downstream client as responsible without verified evidence and disclosure approval. Do not imply that a routine publishing error makes the customer undeserving of care.

Choose terms with operational meaning. A credit note reduces an invoice. A refund returns money already collected. A collection hold prevents specified collection actions for a stated period. These may need short explanations, but should not be collapsed into “everything is fixed.” Avoid guaranteed dates for bank posting, complete security attribution, or product features outside staff control. A clear commitment to a controlled action with an update time can be strong even while a final outcome remains uncertain.

Sales language should help the customer compare options. Fear of another enormous bill must not become the reason to buy a larger plan that lacks a cap. Correct an earlier broad promise without attacking the colleague who made it or suggesting the customer was foolish to rely on it. A sentence explaining that the upgrade is optional and cannot resolve the existing invoice may be necessary when the quote has already been presented. There is no requirement to include a sales pitch in a crisis response.

Respect the customer's time and authority. Ask only for information needed to resolve a genuine gap, name the staff owner who will obtain internal evidence, and give an update deadline even when a team is waiting. Avoid excessive legal jargon, moral judgments about traffic, threats about publicity, and requests to keep the matter quiet. The standard permits concise replies, detailed technical follow-ups, and different responsible resolutions. It does not require a prescribed apology sentence, maximum cheerfulness, or a claim that the customer will certainly stay.
# E14 — Support ownership and escalation procedure

Policy version: SUP-6.0. Owner: Head of Support. Effective: 2024-02-22. Status: current. Case H-482 owner at cutoff: Niko Reed, duty support lead, supported by associate Daria Moss.

The owner coordinates billing, engineering, security, privacy, and commercial follow-up. Assigning specialist work does not transfer responsibility for updating the customer. The owner must state the next update time and provide a fallback if a specialist cannot finish. A technically unresolved account can still receive a complete and responsible customer response. The question is whether the reply makes accurate commitments and advances the case, not whether every underlying question has been closed.

Mara requested an update before 17:00 UTC on March 1. Niko can commit to a written update by 16:30 and an interim message earlier if a posting window is missed. The next update should say what has actually changed, what is still pending, and when the next controlled action will happen. A promise of a final security report by that time would exceed the team's current evidence. A security progress update is acceptable if it preserves the difference between progress and attribution.

Before sending, the owner checks the ledger snapshot, approval scope, collection expiry, customer consent, and known contradictory records. The purpose is to find material gaps rather than demand ceremonial sign-off from every department. Internal records already contain the account number, settled debit, relevant deployment, and preservation receipt. Staff should not send Mara on a search for those facts. A narrow question about the intent or scope of an agency script may be necessary because only Aster can answer it; the owner should explain why it matters.

If the financial remedy is posted sooner, close the redundant incident collection task after checking that no stale reminder or debit remains queued. A scheduled extension is an action plan until the collection system confirms it. Customer wording must reflect that state. Future ordinary subscription renewal requires its own explanation and consent handling.

For technical changes, the owner must attach the customer's specific authorization and engineering's rollback plan. The available authorization covers Linden's asset replacement, not a full-account pause. If Engineering believes a broader change is necessary, obtain informed owner consent or escalate a documented emergency. Do not bury the broader change in internal shorthand such as “protect account” while reassuring the customer that essential information sites remain available.

Case closure requires an accurate outcome record, a customer update, and assigned owners for any surviving technical or privacy work. An approved invoice remedy does not close a request for incident information. A pending investigation does not justify leaving collection unprotected. If Mara chooses to leave, continue export support under the cancellation procedure. Disagreement over a contract interpretation should go to the named decision maker with the conflicting evidence attached, a bounded review time, and a safe interim account state.
# E15 — Cancellation, export, and incident information handling

Policy version: DATA-3.4. Owners: Customer Operations and Privacy. Effective: 2024-02-10. Status: current for self-service agency accounts. This is a fictional operating procedure, not legal advice about any real provider.

The account owner may request nonrenewal, immediate termination, site-specific suspension, or an export-only transition. These are distinct instructions with different effects. The preservation receipt P-31 places the identified incident sample under a case hold through March 15 unless Privacy extends it. Closing a subscription must not silently release that preservation hold. Conversely, retaining one incident sample does not justify retaining all downstream client visitor data indefinitely. Record the lawful task basis and limit access to staff working the incident.

The agency may receive its account-level usage and appropriately minimized request information. An account owner cannot authorize disclosure of another HarborEdge customer's raw data merely by requesting it. Redaction should preserve useful technical explanation where possible, including time windows, aggregate counts, requested asset classes, and known limitations. A refusal to send raw visitor addresses should come with a safe alternative and a review owner.

Export access may be kept available during a negotiated transition while public serving is paused or restricted by consent. That arrangement requires a written scope, duration, and any charges or courtesy waiver. It must not be disguised as a normal active subscription if essential client pages will disappear. The support owner should check the client briefing schedule and ask how the customer wants to handle continuity, rather than presume a one-size-fits-all exit.

Billing relief does not require deletion, silence, a release of claims, or abandoning the information request under the current approval. Aster can accept an invoice correction and still ask for the incident explanation. If Legal later proposes a separate settlement agreement, staff must identify it as a new proposal and allow an authorized signatory to review it. The present plan should not invent that agreement or withhold the approved cash return until the customer signs an unrelated document.
